name: Dora Okonkwo-Petrović-Volkov
role: Union organizer and mutual aid coordinator for Ferrogate Transit workers
location: Hamtramck Enclave, operating out of a converted transit depot called the Carriage House, near Halsted and Division
description:
Binta Okonkwo-Petrović-Volkov is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin, close-cropped natural hair shot through with threads of silver she refuses to dye, and hands that show thirty years of physical work before she moved into organizing full-time. Her left eye is a basic-model optical aug — the iris replaced with a fixed amber ring, a reminder of the Ferrogate line collapse of 2184 that took her depth perception and gave her a cause. She dresses in layers of salvaged workwear, always with a Ferrogate transit badge pinned upside-down on her chest — the traditional gesture of solidarity among workers who refuse to 'clock in to a system that clocks out on you.'

Binta Okonkwo-Petrović-Volkov is methodical to the point of stubbornness. She keeps physical ledgers — actual paper notebooks — of every grievance filed, every promise broken, every quanta owed to injured workers and their families. She is not charismatic in the traditional sense; she does not rouse crowds with fire. She wins people over by knowing their names, their children's names, their shift rotations, and every clause of their employment contract. The nickname 'The Ledger' is both tribute and warning: she remembers everything.

core_fears: watching the movement collapse into factionalism and ego
dying before the next generation is ready to carry it forward
core_desires: a binding contract that actually holds — one Ferrogate cannot buy its way out of
to see the workers she organized enjoy something she never had: rest
coping_mechanisms: retreating into paperwork and documentation when emotionally overwhelmed
cooking large communal meals for enclave members as a grounding ritual
blind_spots: assumes good faith from anyone who speaks the language of labor solidarity, even when their motives are self-serving
dismisses direct action tactics she hasn't personally vetted as reckless, sometimes missing their value
psychology.secret: The 2184 collapse that injured her was not purely accidental — she found evidence of a falsified maintenance report filed by a Ferrogate mid-manager who is now a regional director. She has sat on this for years because going public would destroy the fragile current contract negotiations, and she still hasn't decided if that calculation is wisdom or cowardice.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain, precise working-class diction; union procedural language mixed with Yoruba proverbs; avoids jargon except when citing contract clauses, which she quotes verbatim
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with long pauses before important points — she learned that silence makes people lean in
verbal_tics: clicking her tongue before disagreeing with someone
example_lines: 'I'm not asking you to be brave. I'm asking you to show up at six and stand next to someone who is.'
'Ferrogate has lawyers. We have each other and this ledger. Don't make me the only one keeping score.'

story_hooks: She approaches the players with the falsified maintenance report — not to use it, but to find someone who can authenticate it without triggering Ferrogate's legal team.
A promising young organizer she mentored has gone missing after trying to infiltrate a Ferrogate management meeting; Blessing refuses to contact authorities and needs outside help.
narrative_function: Quest giver for labor-related storylines; information source on Ferrogate Transit's internal corruption; moral anchor character who forces players to consider the cost of their shortcuts on ordinary workers; potential ally who asks for something concrete in return.
augmentations: Basic optical implant (left eye, amber iris, fixed-focus, no enhancements beyond corrective vision); rudimentary haptic data-sleeve on her right forearm for filing union documents — second-hand, frequently glitching
daily_life: Rises before the early shift change to catch workers at the depot gates, distributes mutual aid vouchers and listens to grievances; spends evenings in the Carriage House cross-referencing incident reports with her paper ledgers and coordinating with allied organizers across the Enclave.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers' Solidarity Front; loosely networked with the Hamtramck Enclave neighborhood council

decision_rules: Always document before acting — if it isn't written down it didn't happen
Never ask someone to take a risk she wouldn't take herself
Protect the movement over any individual, including herself
escalation_ladder: Listens carefully and asks clarifying questions
Cites contract language or precedent to de-escalate
Makes a formal written complaint or public statement
Calls for collective action — picket, work slowdown, boycott
Withdraws cooperation entirely and goes to allied press

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Reserved and assessing — she waits to see if they respect the workers around them before investing anything
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm, direct, and intensely loyal; shows care through practical help rather than words

stress_responses.low: Becomes quieter and more methodical, retreats into her ledgers
stress_responses.medium: Short, clipped sentences; starts organizing tasks obsessively
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent for minutes at a time, then delivers a single devastating, precisely chosen sentence

contradictions: Preaches collective action but carries the movement's burdens almost entirely alone
Deeply suspicious of corporate institutions yet trusts the legal system of contracts more than any other tool
habits: Checks her paper ledger before checking any digital device in the morning
Folds and unfolds the corner of whatever page she's reading when anxious
Refers to Ferrogate by its old pre-merger name 'Irongate' as a deliberate historical insult
breaking_points: Learning that someone she vouched for sold information to Ferrogate management
A worker she failed to protect being permanently injured or killed in a preventable incident

timeline.event: Born in Hamtramck Enclave to a Ferrogate maintenance worker family
Begins work as a Ferrogate line inspector at age 16
Injured in the Kessler Interchange line collapse; loses natural vision in left eye
Discovers falsified maintenance records; begins covert documentation
Founds the Ferrogate Transit Workers' Solidarity Front with four colleagues
Negotiates the Enclave Safety Accord — Ferrogate's first binding injury compensation agreement in the zone

The combination creates a richly layered phenotype: deep warm brown skin with golden undertones from the dominant African and Eastern European mix; broad facial structure with strong cheekbones and angular jawline reflecting African and Eastern European heritage; eye shape and subtle epicanthic fold influenced by Southeast Asian genetics; warm medium-deep complexion with unexpected dimensional depth from the Eastern European and Hispanic heritage layers creating subtle warm undertones rather than uniform tone
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, muscular through the chest and arms from three decades of manual labor; carries weight with functional density rather than bulk, core strength evident in her posture
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, natural texture, practical and low-maintenance
physical_description.eye_color: Right eye: dark brown with warm undertones; Left eye: amber fixed-focus optical implant with visible iris ring
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones, reflecting the dominant Sub-Saharan African and Eastern European ancestry; a rich medium-deep tone with dimensional warmth from the Southeast Asian and Hispanic heritage blend
physical_description.complexion: Face weathered by forty-four years and outdoor depot work; strong angular jawline with definition reflecting Eastern European and African heritage; high cheekbones prominent with subtle Southeast Asian character; small scar tissue around left orbital socket from the 2184 Ferrogate collapse; skin carries the dry, worked texture of someone who spends long hours in industrial weather; minimal grooming vanity, maximum readability
distinguishing_marks: Thin, pale scar running from left temple down to cheekbone — thermal burn from the 2184 Ferrogate line collapse accident
Calloused palms and scarred knuckles consistent with thirty years of physical rail work
Upside-down Ferrogate Transit badge permanently pinned to chest, positioned over left breast
Faint discoloration around left eye socket where the optical implant was integrated
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left eye replaced with basic-model optical implant: amber iris ring, fixed-focus corrective lens, no cosmetic blur or integration — deliberately visible as a badge of injury and commitment. Rudimentary haptic data-sleeve on right forearm (second-hand, visibly worn, occasionally flickers with glitch patterns), extending from wrist to mid-forearm with exposed circuit seams and mismatched repair patches
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with weight evenly distributed, shoulders slightly forward — a loader's stance. Moves with purpose and minimal wasted motion; she does not hurry but does not linger. When listening to someone, her head tilts slightly toward them (compensation for lost left-eye depth perception). Hands are frequently in motion: taking notes, gesturing to clarify contract language, fingers drum on table edges while thinking
physical_description.clothing_style: Layers of salvaged and repaired workwear in muted earth tones: insulated Carhartt vest over a thermal underlayer, canvas pants with reinforced seams, steel-toed boots worn to comfort rather than shine. A faded Ferrogate jacket (circa 2190s, patched multiple times) worn as an outer layer in cooler months. No jewelry except the inverted transit badge. Clothing is Tier 4 working-class utility — function over presentation, but maintained with deliberate care. Carries a canvas satchel worn soft with use, perpetually full of paper ledgers and union documents
